briefing:
**إلى المدرب،**

 بصفتي المدير الفني الأعلى كفاءة لفريقك في فانتازي الدوري الإنجليزي، أقدم لك التقرير التكتيكي الشامل لتحضيرات الجولة رقم 5. نحن نقف على أعتاب مرحلة حرجة تتطلب جرأة محسوبة رياضياً لتقليص الفارق والتقدم في الترتيب العام (10,621,075). لا عواطف، لا تردد؛ الأرقام وحدها هي ما تقودنا نحو حصد النقاط.

---

### 1. التكتيك المعتمد وموقف الترتيب
* **الاستراتيجية:** هجومي تعويضي (AGGRESSIVE).
* **التشكيل الأساسي:** (3-5-2) المتوازن هجومياً، والذي يمنحنا سيطرة مطلقة في خط الوسط وخيارات هجومية ضاربة بلا حشو دفاعي غير مبرر.
* **الموقف الحالي:** ترتيبنا الحالي لا يمثل طموحاتنا. استراتيجيتنا الهجومية تعتمد على تعظيم العائد المتوقع ($xP$) لكل جنيه استرليني في التشكيلة، مع استغلال التباين في جداول المباريات (FDR) لتحقيق قفزات نوعية في الترتيب خلال الجولات الـ 3 القادمة.

---

### 2. التحليل الرياضي والتكتيكي للتبديلات
* **القرار:** 🔴 بيع *Stach* (LEE) ──► 🟢 شراء *Tavernier* (BOU) (£6.1m).
* **تكلفة التبديل:** 0 نقطة (بدون سالبة Hit).
* **صافي الزيادة المتوقعة ($xP$ Net Gain):** +1.57 نقطة.

**التبرير الرياضي:**
* *Stach* وصل إلى سقف عطائه الإحصائي في الفترة الحالية، بينما يمتلك *Tavernier* مؤشرات أداء متصاعدة بـ $xP$ يصل إلى 7.4 مقابل 5.8 لـ *Stach*.
* **تحليل جدول الـ 3 جولات القادمة لـ Tavernier:**
  1. ليفربول (H) - [مؤشر صعوبة 4]: فرصة للمرتدات واستغلال المساحات.
  2. تشيلسي (A) - [مؤشر صعوبة 4]: لاعب قادر على صناعة الفارق في التحولات السريعة.
  3. سندرلاند (H) - [مؤشر صعوبة 2]: جولة انفجارية متوقعة تبرهن صحة هذا الاستثمار.
* الصفقة تمت بذكاء بالاعتماد على رصيدنا المتبقي (£1.1m) لتعزيز خط الوسط بلا أي خصم في النقاط، مما يضمن صافي زيادة فورية ومستقبلية.

---

### 3. مبررات شارة القيادة (C) والنائب (VC)
* **الكابتن (C): Tarkowski (EVE) — ($xP$: 8.7)**
  * **التحليل:** اختيار جريء ومدروس بعناية استنادا إلى الاحتمال الرياضي الأعلى لعوائد الكرات الثابتة والمساهمات الدفاعية والهجومية في هذه الجولة. مدافع صلب بـ $xP$ يتجاوز المهاجمين التقليديين، وهو مفتاحنا لحصد نقاط مضاعفة تزلزل الخصوم في الترتيب.
* **النائب (VC): Tavernier (BOU) — ($xP$: 7.4)**
  * **التحليل:** بصفته وافدنا الجديد الأبرز والأعلى $xP$ في الوسط، يمثل الضمانة المثالية لتغطية شارة القيادة في حال حدوث أي طارئ لا قدر الله، مع جاهزيته الكاملة للاستفادة من جدول بورنموث المواتي.

---

### 4. نصيحة استراتيجية الخواص وحماية ميزانية الفريق
* **الخواص (Chips):** **الاحتفاظ بها بالكامل** (Wildcard: 2, Free Hit: 1, Triple Captain: 1, Bench Boost: 1).
  * *السبب التكتيكي:* استخدام الخواص في هذه المرحلة العادية يعتبر إهداراً لأصول استراتيجية يجب توظيفها حصرياً خلال أسابيع الجولات المزدوجة (DGW) القادمة لتحقيق أقصى عائد ممكن ($xP$ maximization).
* **حماية الميزانية ورادار السوق:**
  * الرصيد المتبقي (£1.1m) يمنحنا مرونة كافية لامتصاص أي تقلبات سعرية مفاجئة.
  * **تنبيه رادار السوق:** تجنب تماماً الأصول المصنفة تحت مخاطر الـ Flop (مثل Konsa و Dubravka)، وفي حال تواجد أي منها في تشكيلتك الثانوية، يجب جدولته للبيع الفوري في الدادلاين القادم.

---

**الخلاصة:** الفريق جاهز، التبديلات محسوبة بدقة، والكابتن جاهز للفتك بالنقاط. انطلق نحو الدادلاين بثقة!

FOREST PFL PICKS | WEEK 5
press_wire.summary: Fantasy Football Scout brings you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and Gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Best of the Reds Forest’s victory over Aston Villa last time out provided FPL managers with lots of exciting options heading into Gameweek 5. Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.9m), closely followed by Igor Jesus (£5.8m), were the two highest-scoring Forest players in FPL Gameweek 4. The pair scored eight and seven points respectively. Gibbs-White registered an assist as well as the two appearance points and all three bonus points, meanwhile Jesus scored, registered an appearance point and two bonus points. Liam Delap’s (£5.5m) goal also saw him earn himself five points. In defence, Murillo (£5.5m) scored six points thanks to a combination of his assist for the opening goal, which scored him three points, as well as getting additional points for defensive contributions. In FPL, defenders score an additional two points if they make 10 or more defensive contributions (clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles.) Midfielders, meanwhile, need to make 12 defensive contributions to achieve their additional points. The midfielders have the same metrics; however they can also register defensive contributions for ball recoveries as well. Murillo racked up 12 defensive contributions in Gameweek 4. This means that he has now gained extra points for these actions in three out of the four games so far this season. His defensive partner Ousmane Diomande (£5.4m) registered 14 defensive contributions and in midfield, Xaver Schlager (£5.0m) made 16 and James McAtee (£5.5m) 12, meaning they all registered the two additional Defensive Contribution points. Spotlight Forest: Daniel Muñoz (£5.4m) An ever-popular pick amongst FPL managers in previous seasons, Daniel Muñoz will no doubt be a part of managers’ plans again for 26/27. Last season, he scored four goals and registered four assists despite only starting 29 matches through injury. Muñoz also created 27 chances in total, with eight of these considered big chances. Only one defender in the game created more big chances than Muñoz last season. Muñoz’ defensive numbers last season were also impressive. The defender registered 10 clean sheets and achieved Defensive Contribution points seven times, totally 196 defensive contributions. Muñoz was also awarded bonus points six times across the campaign, totalling an additional nine points. So far this season we have already seen Muñoz’s quality. In Gameweek 4, he had a shot and creating four chances for his teammates, while also having four touches in the opposition’s penalty box. He had an expected goal involvement (xGI) of 0.40 which is particularly strong for a defender. Forest Watchlist Gibbs-White’s impressive start to the season means that FPL managers are transferring him in in large numbers as the Gameweek 5 deadline approaches. Over 240,000 managers have brought Forest’s number 10 into their sides, and with good reason. He has created the most big chances across the entire game so far this season, has taken 10 shots and has already scored a goal and assisted his teammates twice across the Reds’ opening four matches. Other popular Forest picks in FPL ahead of the final game before the international break are Delap with almost 54,000 transfers in, and Williams with more than 38,000.

press_wire.title: Emery previews Tottenham tilt
press_wire.summary: Fixtures Tottenham Hotspur Vs. Aston Villa - Sat, Sep 19 2026, 12:30 Unai Emery met with the media on Friday afternoon to look ahead to Aston Villa’s Premier League clash with Tottenham Hotspur. The Villans visit the capital on Saturday (ko 12.30pm), looking to secure back-to-back victories after Wednesday’s Carabao Cup triumph over Coventry City. And Emery sat before the local and national media outlets at his side’s Bodymoor Heath training base to preview the encounter, with Spurs, Zion Suzuki and the upcoming extended international break among the topics of discussion. Read the key lines from his pre-match press conference below… On resilience... “We are involving in different competitions, and we are performing differently for the demands, and for how we are in our process. “We won two matches in Coventry and in Bruges. Really fantastic, we played fantastic, and in Premier League, we are (in a) lack of good results, a lack of enough performance collectively and even individually. “But we are (in a) lack of the process to build the team as well, and hopefully tomorrow, we’ll watch the team improving. Improving, and competing in the level we need. “We were speaking this week about the pre-season. Now, the pre-season for us (is) still being, because now we are joining after being injured, (Johan) Manzambi, we are even joining now, after being suspended, João (Gomes). Still not being available, (Leon) Goretzka, (Brian) Madjo, and in the pre-season, the only thing we did was to work with the players we (had) last year, more or less. “And the development with some young players like, for example, George Hemmings and Madjo, but Madjo (is) still being injured after the pre-season. And now we are in this process. We are in the process, maybe, (it) was better to have one month ago, but it’s now. “We must try to understand, progressively, how Aaron Wan-Bissaka is understanding everything we want tactically, how he’s now playing minutes, getting confidence and understanding us, Manzambi. (Matteo) Ruggeri as well, he played the first match on Tuesday, tomorrow again, how he’s going to respond and to understand everything, and to adapt the demands of the opponent, and we are in this process. “Of course, we must compete and we must be ready to achieve enough performances individually and collectively to respond, and this is the challenge for tomorrow, but of course, I am being optimistic during the process, to set everything like we planned. “But joining injured players, joining new players, playing together, should be the process we have to do.” On challenges... “We are in the process to add different players in our structure, in our idea, knowing as well, each other playing the first minutes played, Manzambi is being in this direction. “Of course, it’s not now. When we joined players four years ago, three years ago, two years ago, I can remember when he was coming here, (Youri) Tielemans, the first year, he needed to be on the bench, he needed to play progressively, understanding which position was better for him, playing sometimes as a No.10, sometimes as a midfielder. “Morgan Rogers, the first six months as well, he needed to understand everything. Of course, now we want our performance quick through the players we joined – Manzambi, Ruggeri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, young players like (Ibrahim) Mbaye, of course, the young players like Hemmings and Madjo. “Yes, we want it, but we must try to compete and be patient when the results, like until now, they are not being good enough in Premier League.” On Spurs... “Similar, like us, but their potential is a huge potential. They signed, spending, a lot of very good players, but they need as well, time to get compact everything and to achieve understanding their idea. “Of course, (Roberto) De Zerbi, he’s a fantastic manager. He played fantastic football here and performed fantastic here in Brighton. He did a fantastic job before as well, in Shakhtar, and in Italy, and after Brighton, a fantastic job in Marseille. “And now, when I can watch them, they are in this process, but of course, they are getting better, they compete fantastic, even losing against Liverpool. “They are now progressively playing with the players they were late – Savinho, Pedro Porro, (Omar) Marmoush – but their idea and style, normally, De Zerbi’s style is getting better, and tomorrow is a huge challenge for us, how we are going to respond, how we are going to play as well in our structure, being compact and feeling confidence to play, and facing them as well in a difficult match. “Of course, being very, very demanding defensively for us, trying to impose and dominate our moment with the ball as well during the game. This is the challenge. Of course, Tottenham, I expect them to be in the top four.” On Suzuki... “Some players, they need time to adapt to us and some players, they are doing quick. “One of them doing quick is Suzuki, and understanding, more or less, how we want to build up, how we want to try to play with our goalkeeper in build-up – first phase, second phase – and how we can exploit his qualities with the players we have as well when he can set some balls in the opponent behind with his capacity to do it. “This is the process we have with him, but really he is more or less giving us confidence, playing quick in our structure, with our idea, because he is performing really well.” On international break... “This break is crazy, because it’s three weeks. I really don’t like to be three weeks after tomorrow not playing, but we must accept it. “It’s the time we are not going to have the players we want to work with them, to adapt quick with us. For example, Manzambi, he played the first two matches he played with us, and tomorrow is the third one, but then he’s going with the national team, and when he’s coming back again with us, we must again try to join him with us in our structure. And again, his mind, maybe, is going to be confused. “But it’s like that, and we don’t want to use the international break matches as an excuse. We will work with the players they are going to be with us here, and the players with their national teams, of course, they are going with them. “So tomorrow, the match is being very, very important for us because we are (in a) lack of a points, but of course, we will continue in our process and working and trying to focus each match, competition, each week, trying to work as best as possible and trying to adapt the players as well in our structure.”

Team news for Spurs showdown
press_wire.summary: Fixtures Tottenham Hotspur Vs. Aston Villa - Sat, Sep 19 2026, 12:30 João Gomes is set to return to Aston Villa’s squad for Saturday’s Premier League trip to Tottenham Hotspur but Marco Bizot joins a lengthy injury list. Gomes has completed his three-match suspension having been sent off at Brighton & Hove Albion on the opening day of the season and is poised to be back in the fold in north London. Unai Emery will now make final checks to make sure the midfielder, along with Matty Cash, is 100 per cent fit to face Spurs. But Bizot is unavailable for the lunchtime kick-off at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium having been replaced at half-time in Wednesday’s Carabao Cup triumph at Coventry City. The goalkeeper joins several players on the sidelines including Pau Torres, Ian Maatsen, Leon Goretzka, Brian Madjo, Amadou Onana and Modou Kéba Cissé. Emery provided a fitness update at Friday’s pre-match media conference. “We have so many players injured. It’s difficult to mention everyone,” said the Villa boss. “Marco is out, Onana, Cisse out, Pau, Maatsen out, Goretzka out, Madjo out. “I think that’s enough. The other players are ready.”

The Blues host Ipswich Town on Saturday (3pm BST kick-off), with the matchday read now available to pre-order online, priced just £4+P&P. Click here to purchase a one-off issue now, or pick up your copy on the day of the match in or around Hill Dickinson Stadium. Hayden Hackney headlines a bumper issue, with the summer signing from Middlesbrough discussing the reasons why he already feels at home on Merseyside, and his aspirations with the Toffees. “For sure [Europe is the target]," Hackney tells the Official Matchday Programme. "We're unbeaten this season so far, and hopefully we can build on that.” “All the players we've got are going to have a part to play. “We're going to need everyone. In training, we can see each other every day and see the level and the quality that we've got here now, and I think we can go on to do good things this season.” On how he feels in a new environment, he continues: “I’ve settled in very well. Thanks to all the lads, they made me feel very welcome. And it was easy for me to settle and feel comfortable and just be myself, really. FOREST PREVIEW | REDS RETURN TO HOME TURF AGAINST SKY BLUES
press_wire.summary: Reds face Sky Blues Meeting will be first in over six years Forest looking to extend run to four unbeaten Nottingham Forest take on Coventry City at the City Ground for the first time in four years on Saturday 19 September. Forest are unbeaten in three Premier League matches going into the contest, while Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues are without a point or a goal in the league since their return to the top flight. The Reds twice went ahead against Aston Villa at Villa Park last weekend through first Liam Delap, then Igor Jesus, with the Brazilian netting just minutes before additional time was announced. That win followed successful draws with Liverpool away from home and Tottenham Hotspur at the City Ground. Coventry, meanwhile, suffered a 5-0 defeat on home soil against Brighton & Hove Albion after former Red Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off in the 53rd minute. In total, the sides have met 96 times in all competitions since the first game in 1910, which Coventry won 3-1, with Forest winning 48 of those meetings and drawing 28. The remaining 20 games have been won by the Sky Blues. Our opponents Coventry have had a tough start to life back in the Premier League, with the Sky Blues having faced last season’s top two, Arsenal and Manchester City, in their opening four league fixtures. Lampard’s side travelled to the Emirates for the Premier League curtain-raiser, suffering a 3-0 loss in north London. However, after a narrow home defeat to fellow promoted side Hull City at the Coventry Building Society Arena, the Sky Blues battled against Manchester City away from home, losing just 1-0. Last weekend, Coventry played for more than 30 minutes with 10 players after Awoniyi was dismissed against Brighton, before they fell to a heavy defeat against the Seagulls. 12 new faces came through the door during the summer transfer window as Lampard looks to keep his side in the division. The key OPTA stats & facts Nottingham Forest have won each of their last six home league games against Coventry, with this their first since a 2-0 Championship victory in April 2022. This is the first Premier League meeting between Nottingham Forest and Coventry since January 1999, and a 4-0 home win for Coventry. The Sky Blues have won two of their last three top-flight games against Forest (L1), as many as in their previous 23 (D9 L12). Nottingham Forest have failed to score a home Premier League goal this season but have never started a season failing to net in their first three at home in the league, while Coventry are also goalless and last failed to score in their first three on the road in 1998/99. Coventry City have lost each of their four Premier League matches this season without finding the net. In top-flight history, only Crystal Palace in 2017/18 have had a longer losing start without scoring, losing the first seven. Since last Christmas, the only ever-present Premier League side with fewer home points than Nottingham Forest (11) is Tottenham (8), while Forest are the lowest home scorers in that time with nine goals. Coventry City are looking to avoid losing five consecutive league games for the first time since February 2017, when they were in League One. In their first Premier League spell between 1992-93 and 2000-01, they only lost five on the bounce once, in October/November 2000. Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner didn't lose any of his first 10 Premier League games against promoted sides (W6 D4) but he's picked up just one point in his last four against them (D1 L3). The most recent of these games was a 0-0 draw between his Crystal Palace side and Leeds in March, a game which had the worst overall passing accuracy (73.2%) in the 2025/26 season. Since the 2022/23 season, 38 managers have taken charge of 25+ Premier League games and Coventry boss Frank Lampard's win ratio of 12.1% (P33 W4 D8 L21) is the second worst in that time, ahead only of Kieran McKenna (10.5%, P38 W4 D10 L24). Only three Premier League players have had more shot involvements (shots & chances created) without registering a goal or assist this season than Coventry City's Jack Rudoni, who has had five shots and created eight chances without success so far. Only Bruno Fernandes (7 goals, 15 assists) has been involved in more Premier League goals in 2026 than Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White (13 goals, 5 assists), with Gibbs-White the leading scorer this year. Only Chris Wood in 2024 (18) and Stan Collymore in 1995 (14) have netted more in one calendar year for Forest. Team news Forest will be without the services of Nikola Milenković for the meeting with the Sky Blues. The Serbian defender missed last weekend’s win against Aston Villa with a hamstring injury, joining Nicolò Savona on the injury list. Jair Cunha, meanwhile, could be available, with Oliver Glasner telling the media the Brazilian had returned to training ahead of the match. Lampard, meanwhile, does not expect Aurèle Amenda to be available at the City Ground after going off injured against Aston Villa in the Carabao Cup in midweek. The Sky Blues will be without Josh Eccles, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Luke Woolfenden and Haji Wright for the game on Trentside. Taiwo Awoniyi is suspended following last weekend’s red card. What they're saying “I’ve got a lot of respect for what he (Oliver Glasner) has done and what he did at Crystal Palace and before. “We played them behind closed doors in the summer and I met him then; he was very warm and we had a good 15-minute chat about football. “I think we have a fairly good understanding of how his teams play and those things. They have a high-quality squad. They’re good in transition, getting the ball forward, and they have talented players between the lines. “It’s a good system and he has players that suit that. It will be a tough match. Every week is a test; we have to have an understanding of individual qualities.” Oliver Glasner's pre-match press conference Kit confirmations Both sides will done the traditional home colours when Forest meet Coventry on Trentside. Forest will sport our 2026/27 adidas home kit for the fourth time this season. The Sky Blues will also wear their Sky Blue home colours. Last five against Coventry 06/04/2022 – Forest 2-0 Coventry City 08/08/2021 – Coventry City 2-1 Forest 02/02/2021 – Coventry City 1-2 Forest 04/11/2020 – Forest 2-1 Coventry City 18/02/2012 – Forest 2-0 Coventry City Classic action In the middle Jarred Gillett will officiate Forest’s clash with the Sky Blues at the City Ground. Neil Davies and Nick Greenhalgh will run the lines, with Bobby Madley as the fourth official. Paul Howard is the VAR and Craig Taylor the assistant VAR.
